sovereign_country.strategic_role: 连接拉美市场的欧洲商贸桥梁、本地化仓配与数字游民签证

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Construction of Thermal Multi-Stage Flash and Membrane Desalination

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: EU–Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA, 2017)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo, as amended by Ley 11/2021, de 9 de julio; Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo, approving the AML/CFT Regulation; Real Decreto 1098/2017, de 29 de diciembre, establishing the Registro de Titularidades Reales (UBO register) and amending the Commercial Registry Regulations; transposition of Directive (EU) 2018/843 (Fifth AML Directive).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Criminal Record Certificate (Certificado de Antecedentes Penales) of foreign director or shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent judicial or administrative authority of the country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney (Poder) granted by a foreign corporate shareholder for the Spanish incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Good Standing (Certificado de Registro / Vigencia) of the foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the EU Consolidated Sanctions List (CFSP), UN Security Council sanctions, the Spanish SEPBLAC/preventive list, and, for USD transactions, the OFAC SDN list. Politically exposed persons (PEPs) are defined under Law 10/2010, art. 12, and SEPBLAC Guidance Directive 1/2012; enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification, and senior management approval are required. Continuous monitoring applies to beneficial owners, directors, and shareholders.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry) – online name certification service at https://www.rmc.es/ or through authorized Spanish notaries
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be in Spanish or any co-official Spanish language (Catalan, Basque, Galician). Non-Latin scripts require transliteration into the Spanish Latin alphabet in accordance with official orthographic rules. The corporate form must be expressed as 'Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada' or the abbreviation 'S.L.'; foreign equivalents are not accepted. Names must not be misleading, contrary to public order, or produce phonetic identity with an existing registered entity.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the negative name certificate (Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social) is denied, the applicant may file a written 'recurso de alzada' before the Dirección General de los Registros y del Notariado (DGRN) within one month from notification, specifying the grounds of rejection. Alternatively, a 'recurso contencioso-administrativo' may be lodged with the Audiencia Nacional within two months. Practically, a fresh application with a modified name may be submitted to the Registro Mercantil Central immediately; the administrative fee for the negative certificate is non-refundable.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is initially permissible only if the statutory registered office is a physical address in Spain capable of receiving notifications and legal service. For ISIC 4322 seawater desalination EPC projects, a virtual office alone does not satisfy commercial-substance expectations of the tax administration, labour authorities, or the Ministry for Ecological Transition; a physical management or project office within Spain should be maintained.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for newly incorporated SLs without PEP or sanctions indicators; estimated at under 10% per audit year for commercial substance inspection, increasing to approximately 30% if UBO verification discrepancies or sanctions list matches are detected.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social (name clearance search and reservation)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff currently €13.80 according to RMC fee schedule; may change annually.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial fees for incorporation deed (Escritura de Constitución), including statutory attestation and capital deposit verification
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary of the chosen registered office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Ministerially set notarial tariff applied to share capital and number of deed clauses; market benchmark for a standard SL with €3,000 capital.
Statutory tariff under Royal Decree 1219/1986 and updated annual rates; benchmark for standard SL registration.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT pre-incorporation UBO identification and PEP/sanctions screening dossier preparation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External legal counsel or specialised compliance firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a low-risk EPC construction entity; includes UBO declaration, sanctions screening, and verification.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: BORME publication fee (Boletín Oficial del Registro Mercantil)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Agencia Estatal Boletín Oficial del Estado

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille and notarization of foreign corporate/shareholder documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foreign competent authority (e.g., Secretary of State / Ministry of Foreign Affairs) and Spanish Consulate if consular legalization
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per document; varies by jurisdiction (apostille from $10–$50 per document plus translation/notary fees).

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 approving the consolidated text of the Spanish Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), particularly Articles 19-23 (incorporation deed and bylaws), Articles 28-30 (founders), Articles 58-62 (capital contributions), Articles 209-252 (company administration), and Articles 279-283 (annual accounts filing). Law 14/2013 and Law 18/2022 provide electronic incorporation and reduced-capital rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The competent Registro Mercantil Provincial for the province of the registered office, coordinated through the Central Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Central) for name clearance.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public deed of incorporation (escritura pública de constitución), including the articles of association, followed by an application for registration with the competent Provincial Mercantile Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The minimum share capital of a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada is EUR 1. The capital must be fully subscribed and paid on incorporation. Until equity reaches EUR 3,000, at least 20% of annual profit must be allocated to legal reserve until the reserve plus capital reaches EUR 3,000, and shareholders have supplementary liability up to the difference between EUR 3,000 and subscribed capital upon liquidation. A bank certificate is not required if the founders expressly assume joint and several liability for the existence of the contributions. Notarial, Mercantile Registry, name-reservation, publication, translation, and local administrative charges remain payable; Spain has no single uniform state incorporation filing fee.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Board resolves that: (1) the Company accepts the subscription and full payment of its share capital as recorded in the incorporation deed and approves the resulting ownership schedule; (2) the registered office at the address stated in the deed is adopted for all statutory purposes; (3) [Name] is appointed Sole Director, or, if a board structure is adopted, [Names] are appointed directors, each accepting office and declaring no legal disqualification; (4) [Name] is appointed secretary, if applicable; and (5) the officers are authorized to complete Mercantile Registry, tax, banking, licensing, and electronic-signature filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Central Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Central), online name-certification portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit up to five proposed names, identifying the intended legal form as Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada. Obtain the negative name certificate and reserve the approved name for the statutory validity period. Execute a power of attorney if the filing is made by counsel.
required_dossiers: Foreign corporate documents, apostilled or legalized and translated into Spanish where required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name is rejected, submit an alternative name or challenge the refusal through the Registry's available administrative or judicial review procedures. Correct identity, translation, or authorization defects before resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorizing Spanish notary public (notaría) and, where applicable, the CIRCE/PAE electronic business-creation channel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the articles of association, corporate purpose, registered office, share capital, share allocation, governance model, director appointments, and beneficial-owner information. Foreign founders must obtain Spanish tax identification numbers (NIE/NIF) and provide legalized corporate authority documents. Arrange a bank capital certificate or include the statutory founder declaration accepting contribution liability.
required_dossiers: Foreign shareholder corporate extracts, constitutional documents, apostille or legalization, and sworn Spanish translation
Bank certificate of capital deposit or founder contribution-liability declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Cure notarial observations by amending the draft deed, supplying missing legalization or translation, or correcting beneficial-owner and tax-identification information before execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the public deed of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish notary public selected by the founders
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear personally or through a notarized representative. Execute the public incorporation deed, articles, share subscription statement, director acceptance, and beneficial-owner declaration. Ensure the corporate purpose expressly covers desalination engineering, construction, commissioning, operation support, water infrastructure, and ancillary activities, subject to required public permits.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request a corrective or supplementary notarial deed for clerical, identity, capital, governance, or corporate-purpose defects. Re-execute where the notary identifies a material validity defect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain tax identification and commence registry filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria) and the competent Provincial Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the provisional NIF using Form 036 and submit the deed electronically or through the notary to the Provincial Mercantile Registry. Pay applicable notarial and registry charges. After registration, obtain the definitive NIF and update the Tax Agency with the registered deed and final corporate details.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a qualification notice, correct the identified defect within the applicable validity period, submit a corrected deed or supplementary document, and request requalification. An adverse qualification may be appealed to the Directorate-General for Legal Security and Public Faith or challenged before the competent court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete post-registration corporate and tax formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Tax Agency, Provincial Mercantile Registry, Social Security General Treasury, and relevant labour authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the definitive NIF, activate electronic notifications, register the company for applicable VAT and business activities, legalize accounting and corporate books electronically, and register as an employer before hiring personnel. Adopt the first board or sole-director resolutions and establish accounting, invoicing, AML, health-and-safety, and data-protection controls.
required_dossiers: Corporate books and accounting-book legalization file
Employer registration documents, if personnel will be hired
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct rejected tax, Social Security, electronic-book, or beneficial-owner submissions through the relevant portal and preserve submission receipts. Rectify missed filings through late-registration procedures and assess applicable penalties or surcharges.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Secure project-specific construction, water, environmental, and operating approvals
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Relevant Autonomous Community industry and environmental authority, competent river-basin authority, Directorate-General for the Coast and the Sea where applicable, municipality, and project-specific utility regulators
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before construction or operation, determine the plant site, capacity, intake and discharge route, energy equipment, chemical storage, waste streams, and public-domain occupation. Obtain the applicable environmental assessment, water-concession or authorization, discharge authorization, coastal authorization or concession, municipal planning and works permit, activity or environmental license, industrial commissioning notification, and waste, chemical, pressure-equipment, electrical, fire, and occupational approvals.
required_dossiers: Marine outfall and diffuser design, if applicable
Energy, electrical, pressure-equipment, and fire-safety certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to deficiency notices within the stated deadline, revise technical studies, conduct required public-information procedures, and submit supplementary environmental or hydraulic evidence. Administrative appeals and judicial review remain available against refusals, subject to statutory deadlines.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: The Industry Directorate or equivalent industrial authority of the relevant Autonomous Community, together with the municipality, competent river-basin authority, Autonomous Community environmental authority, and coastal authority where applicable. Spain has no single national desalination-plant licensing board.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Applicable municipal environmental or activity license and construction/works permit, together with the Autonomous Community industrial commissioning or operating notification/registration, water-concession or authorization, discharge authorization, and coastal public-domain concession or authorization where required. The exact titles vary by Autonomous Community and site.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: The environmental body designated by the relevant Autonomous Community under Law 21/2013 on Environmental Assessment; the Ministry for the Ecological Transition and the Demographic Challenge may act as the competent body for state-competence projects.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Site- and project-dependent. A desalination plant may require ordinary or simplified environmental impact assessment under Law 21/2013, particularly where marine works, protected areas, significant water abstraction or discharge, large capacity, or associated infrastructure are involved. The competent environmental body must issue the screening or assessment determination before construction. No universal exemption applies.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with the Water Act consolidated by Royal Legislative Decree 1/2001, Royal Decree 849/1986 and applicable basin plans for discharges, and the conditions of the discharge authorization. Brine and other effluents must meet authorization-specific flow, salinity, temperature, chemical, ecological, and monitoring limits; marine discharges must satisfy coastal and marine environmental conditions. Hazardous waste, chemicals, oils, membranes, sludge, and packaging must be managed under Law 7/2022 and implementing waste rules. VOC and combustion emissions, if any, are subject to the applicable Autonomous Community air-quality permit and emission limits. There is no single national numerical brine threshold applicable to every site.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain municipal or regional fire-safety approval under the applicable building and fire-safety rules, including the Spanish Building Code and the Regulation on Fire Safety in Industrial Establishments where applicable. Complete structural, geotechnical, seismic, electrical, pressure-equipment, lifting-equipment, and occupational-risk assessments before commissioning. Comply with Law 31/1995 on Occupational Risk Prevention, coordinate contractor activities, certify emergency plans, provide worker training and personal protective equipment, and register or inspect regulated installations through authorized control bodies when required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); electronic portal: Sede Electrónica de la AEAT (https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es); customs platform: Declaración Sumaria de Depósito Temporal / Ventanilla Única Aduanera.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity that begins taxable activity in Spain must obtain a NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) before commencing operations. For non-resident entities without a permanent establishment, apply for an NIF for non-residents (model 030) through an appointed tax representative with Spanish residence if the entity is established outside the EU/EEA. For a Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL), a provisional CIF/NIF is issued at public deed registration before the Commercial Registry; final NIF is obtained via form 036/037 within 10 working days after integration of capital, accompanied by the deed, bylaws, proof of appointment of administrator, and Spanish bank account certificate. VAT registration (Código de Operaciones Económicas, IAE activity code 4322) is mandatory and must be declared on form 036 before invoicing. Foreign sub-contractors executing EPC works in Spain must register for NIF even if zero-rated supplies are intended, to file periodic VAT returns and furnish documentation to the principal contractor under the reverse-charge mechanism where applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; territorial scope: worldwide taxation for tax-resident SL on corporate income tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades); non-resident shareholders taxed only on Spanish-source income. No tax-haven exemption zone applies to a standard SL.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain generally does not permit check-the-box pass-through treatment for an SL; the SL is an autonomous corporate taxpayer subject to 25% corporate income tax (reduced 15% for newly created entities under the Spanish Corporate Income Tax Law Article 29.1, subject to conditions). Elections available: optional consolidated tax group regime (Grupo de Consolidación Fiscal) under Articles 55-75 of the Corporate Income Tax Law; accelerated depreciation or free depreciation for environmentally friendly investments (including water desalination assets under the Circular Economy incentives); VAT grouping regime in the Basque Country only, not for peninsular Spain; equity kicker tax credit (reserva de capitalización) election. Hybrid mismatch rules per ATAD (Law 18/2022) constrain interest deduction elections; no specific Spanish 'check-the-box' statutory election exists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (IVA / Spanish VAT), governed by Ley 37/1992 and RD 1624/1992, harmonized with EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general exemption threshold for establishment; any entity performing taxable supplies in mainland Spain or Balearic Islands must register for VAT even for a single transaction. For intra-EU distance sales of goods and cross-border telecommunications/broadcasting/e-services, the €10,000 annual EU-wide threshold permits suppliers to use the Union One Stop Shop (OSS) instead of multi-country registration. For imports (including desalination plant equipment), there is no registration threshold; customs import VAT is paid at clearance unless a deferred VAT accounting authorization is granted.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Real-time fiscal information reporting via the SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) applies to large enterprises — taxable persons with turnover exceeding €6,010,121.04, all entities in consolidated VAT groups, and those under the refund regime of Article 35.IV LIVA — in which invoice transaction records must be transmitted electronically to AEAT within 4 calendar days of issue or receipt (8 days for certain EDI invoices) using XML through certified web services (API) or a Standard Audit File Tax (SAFT) integrated system. Digital stamping of invoices is not mandatory; however, under the 'Crea y Crece' Law 18/2022, all B2B invoices must be issued electronically in an interoperable structured format, and billing software must comply with the 'Verifactu' technical specification guaranteeing integrity, legibility, traceability, and third-party verification. Failure to comply with SII deadlines produces a fine of €250 per omission up to €6,000, and use of non-certified software may trigger a penalty of as much as 40% of the value of transactions recorded.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods requiring physical export from Spain/EU to a non-EU destination qualify for the full exemption with right to deduct input VAT (Art. 21 LIVA) provided the goods leave the EU within 3 months from dispatch (extension possible up to 12 months with justified customs or transport delays). Construction-related services embedded in exported goods (e.g., fabrication/installation of desalination machinery destined for third states) can qualify as zero-rated 'directly related to export of goods' only when the services are performed in Spain on goods being exported and the services do not lose their link to the exported goods. Offshore services physically or economically rendered outside the EU are exempt under Art. 69 LIVA (services linked to immovable property located abroad) where the EPC contract covers construction and installation works at a foreign desalination site; such services are zero-rated but subject to documented evidence of the place-of-supply rules. For a Spanish SL executing EPC works in Spain for a non-EU client but delivering a plant within Spain, standard 21% VAT generally applies unless the goods are simultaneously exported.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Single Administrative Document (DUA) / customs export declaration duly accepted by Spanish Customs (registration code, Aduana, date, and customs office of exit)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill or CMR consignment note showing the Spanish exporter as consignor and the non-EU buyer as consignee

Inward Remittance Certificate or bank transfer evidence (SWIFT MT103) proving that the foreign exchange proceeds from the export sale have been repatriated and credited to the Spanish exporter's account (required for deduction under the export refund regime)
Commercial invoice, packing list, and contract (EPC/purchase order) identifying the goods, quantum, unit values, and payment terms
Customs exit confirmation (BBDD 'BAE' — Bail) demonstrating actual exit from Spanish/EU customs territory

Proof of transport contract (freight contract, shipping agent certificate) naming the Spanish exporter, and where the value exceeds certain thresholds, a certificate from a Spanish customs agent or shipping company
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT audits export VAT documentation with heightened scrutiny of zero-rating claims, particularly where the exporter fails to produce the customs exit certificate, B/L, or foreign exchange settlement within the verification phase. Failure to substantiate the export within the legal time limit (generally 3 months with possible extension, plus the FX repatriation requirement per the Spanish Tax Law and Central Bank norms) triggers a VAT assessment with statutory interest (late-payment interest currently 4.0625% for 2025, updated annually), plus a surcharge for late payment without prior assessment: 5%, 10%, 15%, or 20% depending on delay. Tax fraud penalties for false export claims range from 50% to 150% of the tax defrauded, with aggravating factors for means of impediment (ocultación, use of fake documents). For knowingly fraudulent export zero-rating or fictitious exports, the responsible parties incur criminal tax evasion liability under Art. 305 of the Spanish Criminal Code (penalties of imprisonment of 1 to 5 years and tax fine of up to 6 times the defrauded amount) when the amount exceeds €120,000 per tax period. Retrospective clawback also applies to refunded input VAT previously credited, and professional fiscal representatives or customs agents may be jointly and severally liable for damages. Additionally, the SL's administrative body may face a remedial penalty under Art. 40 of Act 11/2021 for non-compliance with the anti-abuse rules substituting the beneficiary owner in export transactions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), as part of the European System of Central Banks, with delegated supervisory and regulatory functions for foreign exchange, capital controls, and external transactions; the Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones (DGCI) within the Ministry of Economy handles foreign investment registry filings; the Spanish AML authority (SEPBLAC) and the Comisión de Prevención del Blanqueo de Capitales enforce compliance in the banking channel.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain, as a eurozone member, maintains fully liberalised current and capital account convertibility under Articles 63–65 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and the OECD Capital Movements Liberalisation Code. There are no exchange controls or foreign-exchange rationing measures. Profit and capital remittances (dividends, interest, loan repayments, liquidation proceeds, royalties, EPC milestone payments) can be freely repatriated without prior administrative authorisation. The only hurdles are non-FX documentary: compliance with corporate tax withholding and reporting (Modelo 216/217 for dividends and interest, Modelo 210 for non-resident income), registration of the foreign investment in the Spanish Foreign Investment Registry, availability of tax-residency certificates and beneficial-ownership certificates under applicable Double Taxation Treaties, and bank-level AML/KYC screening, including source-of-funds and beneficial-ownership details on any wire exceeding EUR 10,000.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender regime exists in Spain. Exporters of goods or services, including desalination EPC works, are permitted to retain all export proceeds in freely convertible foreign currency or convert to euros at their discretion; the statutory conversion ratio is zero (0%). For balance-of-payments statistical purposes, export settlements must be reported to the Banco de España; when proceeds are received through a resident bank, the bank reports automatically through the External Transactions Registry. For any export settlement collected outside Spain, the Spanish resident exporter must directly file the corresponding balance-of-payments declaration (form BOE-P2) within the first ten working days of the month following the settlement. No prescribed surrender timeline applies because no conversion is required.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium for EU/EEA licensed Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) that hold a passport for Spain under PSD2, and Low for offshore, non-EEA digital EMIs. An EEA EMI can offer operational cash accounts for milestone disbursements and supplier payments, but it cannot serve as a settlement bank for project financing, capital escrow accounts, or documentary letters of credit. Offshore digital EMIs headquartered in the United Kingdom after Brexit, or in non-EU jurisdictions, lack passporting rights; they must obtain a separate Spanish e-money institution licence or operate through a Spanish bank agent, which is commercially and regulatory burdensome. Consequently, using an offshore EMI for the SL's treasury is not viable; the EPC project's liquidity must be maintained through a conventional Spanish credit institution with full correspondent banking capabilities.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively mandatory for the SL's authorized signatories and, where significant ownership is held by non-residents, for at least one director or a specially appointed attorney-in-fact. Spanish tier-1 banks require a personal interview at a locally registered branch before providing a fully operative account, particularly for escrow accounts and for any account receiving more than EUR 50,000 in initial capital. Remote onboarding with video conferencing is permitted only when the company has prior banking relations with the same banking group or when all directors and beneficial owners hold EU electronic identification; for a foreign EPC parent driving a desalination project, the bank will require an in-person branch meeting or, alternatively, a notarized power of attorney granted before a Spanish notary (or a foreign notary with apostille) to a resident manager who appears physically at the branch. The Registered Office must be physically verified and the beneficial-owner declaration must be filed with the Registro Mercantil.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner or director resident in a high-risk jurisdiction or appears on PEP (politically exposed person) lists.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full accreted corporate registry extracts of the SL and each parent entity, notarized and apostilled certified passport of every signatory and shareholder holding >10%; European PEP declaration form; source of wealth and source of funds statements; sworn statement of sound business reputation; tax residency certificates; sanction-screening clearance letters; and a bank reference letter from the introducing correspondent bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial equity injection from a foreign shareholder in an amount inconsistent with the SL's minimum capital or operational needs.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital increase resolution recorded in the Corporate Book; notarized share-purchase agreement executed by the foreign shareholder; the Iberian Society bank statement with the source of funds; the EPC project-financing letter evidencing the capital call schedule; the Spanish corporate income tax filing and Central Balance-Sheet data; and a formal declaration of the transaction under the Spanish Foreign Investment regime.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid outbound payment chain to subcontractors or material suppliers in third countries without established trade background.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed EPC subcontracts and purchase orders with commencement certificates; commercial invoices and final acceptance certificates; proof of delivery under Incoterms or the Chamber of Commerce certificate of origin; SWIFT MT103 evidence reflecting the same payment purpose; and transfer pricing documentation for any intra-group flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of intermediate shell entities or opaque ownership chains with nominee shareholders.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified chain-of-ownership diagram showing every entity from the ultimate human beneficial owner to the Spanish SL; audited financial statements of all intermediate entities; registered address and substance details for each entity; bank verification letters for each entity's operating account; compliance with the Spanish Central Beneficial Owner Registry (RCR) final filing status; and a statutory declaration that no funds are derived from tax havens or battery of illegal activities.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections for the Spanish SL (equity contributions, share premium, latent subordinated shareholder loans) must be routed through an SWIFT MT103 or MT202/202COV for USD-denominated injections or a TARGET2/SEPA cash transfer for EUR-denominated injections. The bank transfer must include a correctly classified purpose code under the Banco de España's balance-of-payments nomenclature; the code will identify either a direct foreign investment in equity of a resident company or a financial loan granted by a non-resident to a resident. The SL must submit to its Spanish bank the notarial certificate of the capital increase (or equivalent deed of contribution), the updated Commercial Registry certificate, the foreign investment declaration form when the invested amount exceeds EUR 3,000,000 (filed with the DGCI), and a letter from the ultimate beneficial owner confirming source of funds. The receiving bank will verify the purpose code against the SL's disclosed corporate activity (ISIC 4322), and if the funds are expressly destined for a project escrow, they will be blocked for milestone utility and disbursed only against project-stage approvals.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The primary clearing rail for outbound trade disbursements will be SWIFT MT103 for suppliers and subcontractors who need direct bank-to-bank crediting; for very high-value settlements above EUR 1 million or for non-euro USD clearing, SWIFT MT202COV will be used through a correspondent bank. For imports of desalination membranes, pressure vessels, pumps, and thermal fixtures, the EPC contractor will use commercial documentary letters of credit issued under the ICC UCP 600 (and ISBP 745, where applicable) through a Spanish issuing bank, with the beneficiary's presenting bank acting as confirming or negotiating bank. All intra-EU euro disbursements will be cleared through SEPA CT (ISO 20022 payment instruction), while Spanish large-value euro payments may utilise TARGET2 real-time gross settlement when same-day completion is contractually mandated. Each outbound payment will require a matching progress invoice, works certificate, or despatch document; the bank will conduct an AML transactional check against the UN/EU sanctions list and will require the underlying EPC schedule to verify the commercial realism of payment frequency.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable outright forward FX contracts (EUR/USD, EUR/CNH and other freely convertible pairs) with tenors aligned to the engineering-procurement-construction (EPC) cash-flow curve, executed under an industry-standard ISDA/2002 (or Spanish standard documentation), with the Spanish SL or its project finance SPV as counterparty

Cross-currency swaps (XCS) for hedging long-term project finance debt service or for converting non-euro liabilities into EUR fixed/floating obligations, subject to the CRR and EMIR clearing and margining rules

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for offshore-pegged or illiquid emerging-market currencies (e.g., North African dinar, GCC currencies, or MXN) used on a cash-settlement basis where physical delivery is impossible or inefficient

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Modelo 390 - Annual VAT reconciliation return (Declaracion resumen anual del IVA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1-30 following the calendar fiscal year end (by 30 Jan Y+1)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge (recargo) of 5% to 20% plus statutory late-payment interest; fraud penalty of 50% to 150% of the amount due (Art. 191 LGT); minimum formal-defect fine of EUR 200.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Modelo 347 - Annual statement of transactions with third parties exceeding EUR 3,005.06 per counterparty
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: February 1-28 following the reporting calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of EUR 300 minimum for non-filing; 1% of omitted amounts above the threshold (minimum EUR 150, maximum EUR 6,000) for inaccurate or incomplete data (Art. 199 LGT).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Modelo 200 - Annual Corporate Income Tax return (Impuesto sobre Sociedades)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days following the six-month post-year-end period; calendar fiscal year: by July 25
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Extemporaneous filing surcharge of 5% (within 3 months) up to 20% (over 12 months) plus late-payment interest; tax penalty of 50% to 150% of the underpaid amount (Art. 191 LGT).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Telematic legalization of statutory accounting books (Libro Diario and Libro de Inventarios y Cuentas Anuales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil territorial where the SL is domiciled
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months of fiscal year end; calendar fiscal year: by April 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unlegalized books lose probative value in commercial litigation (Art. 27-28 Codigo de Comercio); registry may reject subsequent annual filings; formal compliance burden continues regardless.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (Junta General Ordinaria) approving annual accounts, audit report, and appropriation of results
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Collective corporate body; minutes recorded in the Libro de Actas
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of fiscal year end; calendar fiscal year: by June 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Joint and several liability of directors for damages caused by failure to convene or approve the accounts in time; persistent inactivity triggers compulsory dissolution grounds (Art. 363 LSC).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual accounts (Deposito de Cuentas Anuales) at the Mercantile Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil territorial where the SL is registered
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month of approval of the annual accounts; calendar fiscal year: by July 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000 under Ley 14/2013; 6 months after the fiscal year end the registry closes the corporate sheet (cierre de hoja registral), blocking registration of all new corporate acts; sustained non-compliance leads to administrative strike-off (Art. 283 LSC).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO declaration (Declaracion de Titularidad Real / SITURE) attached to the deposit of annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil / Colegio de Registradores (SITURE system)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed together with the annual accounts deposit (calendar fiscal year: by July 30); any change in ultimate beneficial ownership must be filed within 1 month of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: AML fines up to EUR 60,005 for omission or outdated UBO information (Ley 10/2010); filing blocks on registry procedures until the declaration is corrected.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: IAE (Impuesto sobre Actividades Economicas) municipal annual quota, payable where annual turnover exceeds EUR 1,000,000
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Billed under the municipal tax calendar; principal installment due in September-November of the tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Municipal coercive collection proceedings; surcharge of 5% to 20% on late payment; denial of the certificate of tax clearance (certificado de estar al corriente) required for public tenders and EPC contract awards.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit unless, for two consecutive fiscal years, the SL meets at least two of the following three size exemption tests under Art. 263 Ley de Sociedades de Capital: (i) balance-sheet total not exceeding EUR 4,000,000; (ii) net annual turnover not exceeding EUR 8,000,000; (iii) average workforce not exceeding 50 employees. An ISIC 4322 desalination EPC company will ordinarily exceed the EUR 8,000,000 turnover test, making the statutory audit compulsory; audit is also mandatory when the SL consolidates within a group or acts as a regulated public-works concessionaire.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Individual annual accounts under the Spanish General Accounting Plan (PGC, Real Decreto 1514/2007, updated by Real Decreto 1/2021), equivalent to Spanish Local GAAP for SL entities; mandatory IFRS-EU (Reg. (EC) 1606/2002) applies only to consolidated accounts of listed groups.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SL must annually confirm its ultimate beneficial owners to the Mercantile Registry, filed through the SITURE platform together with the deposit of annual accounts. UBO means any natural person directly or indirectly holding more than 25% of the share capital or voting rights, or exercising control over the SL (Ley 10/2010; Real Decreto 304/2014). Any share transfer that changes UBO status must be declared within 1 month of the corporate act, and breaches are sanctioned under the AML regime with fines up to EUR 60,005.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Libro Registro de Socios (Register of Members)
Libro de Actas de la Junta General (Minutes Book of General Meetings)
Libro de Actas del Consejo de Administracion (Board Minutes Book, if a board exists)
Libro de Inventarios y Cuentas Anuales (Inventory and Annual Accounts Book)
Libro Registro de Contratos (Register of Contracts with Sole Shareholder, if applicable)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$250-US$1,500 per year for registered-office domiciliation services and a gestoria corporate compliance package in Spain
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$12,000-US$30,000 per year for a statutory audit of a mid-sized to large desalination EPC 'Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada' with turnover above the EUR 8,000,000 audit-exemption threshold

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (tipo general of the Spanish corporate income tax under Law 27/2014, Ley del Impuesto sobre Sociedades)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Newly created entities, including S.L. structures, benefit from a 15% reduced rate for the first two tax periods in which they obtain a positive taxable base, subject to activity and capitalisation conditions; further incentives include R&D and technological innovation tax credits, deductions for reinvestment of extraordinary profits, the capitalisation reserve, and special regimes for patent boxes and export activities.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite (no statutory expiration; annual offset is limited to 50%-70% of the positive tax base depending on net turnover, with a minimum protected offset amount of EUR 1,000,000 for taxpayers subject to the limitation)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 – Declaración del Impuesto sobre Sociedades, submitted electronically via the Spanish Tax Agency AEAT website (Sede Electrónica de la AEAT) using an authorised electronic certificate or user credential
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly advance tax filings (Modelo 202/222) are also mandatory during the tax period for entities subject to fractional payments
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual Modelo 200 must be filed within 25 calendar days immediately following the six months after the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year taxpayer the deadline is generally 25 July of the following year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Entity identification: NIF (tax ID), legal name, registered address, and fiscal year covered
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: N/A for non-resident shareholders; the resident S.L. is the filing taxpayer. Non-residents without a permanent establishment in Spain must instead file the non-resident income tax return, generally Modelo 210.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit before tax (resultado contable antes de impuestos); must reconcile with the financial statements accepted at the general meeting
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: N/A; this box captures the Spanish-resident entity's own worldwide accounting result. Non-residents should not report this item on Modelo 200.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Permanent and temporary adjustments to accounting profit: depreciation, amortisation, provisions, transfer-pricing corrections, tax-exempt income, and other extra-accounting adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: N/A; non-resident contractors invoicing the Spanish entity do not enter adjustments on Modelo 200. Their income is reportable under IRNR in Spain if the income source is Spanish territory and no double-tax treaty relief applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compensation of previous negative tax bases (BIN), applicable within the carryforward and annual offset limitations
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: N/A for non-resident shareholders. A non-resident entity that is not fiscally resident in Spain cannot use a Spanish S.L.'s loss carryforwards.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base (base imponible) resulting from accounting profit adjusted by the entries in Boxes 003 and 004
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: N/A; the taxable base belongs exclusively to the resident S.L. Non-resident recipients of Spanish-source dividends are taxed at the withholding level rather than on this form.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross tax liability (cuota íntegra) after applying the statutory rate (25%, or 15% for qualifying new entities) to the taxable base
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: N/A; this is the resident entity's tax calculation. Non-resident dividends and interest are subject to withholding as seen in the profit repatriation section, not to progressive CIT rates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions, bonuses, double-taxation credits, and prepayments (deducciones, bonificaciones y pagos fraccionados) applied against the gross tax liability
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: N/A; non-residents do not claim deductions on the resident entity's Modelo 200. Treaty relief for foreign recipients is sought via withholding reduction, exemption, or refund mechanisms.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final net tax due (cuota líquida resultante), reflecting amounts payable to AEAT or refundable to the company
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: N/A; the ultimate foreign shareholder has no direct filing right or obligation on the resident company's net tax position.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Modelo 200 triggers recargos extemporáneos: 5% surcharge for filings within three months of the deadline, 10% for up to six months, 15% for up to twelve months, and 20% after twelve months, plus default interest; if AEAT issues a formal demand, fixed penalties of EUR 1,000 to EUR 20,000 apply. Understated taxable income may additionally be punished with late-payment penalties between 50% and 150% of the evaded amount under Ley General Tributaria (art. 191).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 21% (IRNR general withholding on dividends distributed by a Spanish S.L. to a non-resident shareholder)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident shareholder must provide an up-to-date Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) issued by the shareholder's tax authority, apostilled/legalised where required, to the Spanish paying company before the dividend distribution; the Spanish company may then apply the reduced treaty rate or, in an EU parent-subsidiary case, the 0% rate provided the EU holding conditions are met (at least 10% shareholding, one year holding period, and no treaty shopping). If tax was withheld at the full 21%, the non-resident may file Modelo 210 with AEAT within the four-year refund window together with the TRC and supporting dividend documentation to claim the excess. AEAT may also require form 296 (annual non-resident withholding return) reconciliation by the distributing entity.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory IRNR withholding: 24% on royalties (cánones), 21% on interest and other financial income; zero rate for interest/royalty payments to associated EU/EEA resident companies under Directive 2003/49/EC where the qualifying participation and beneficial ownership conditions are fulfilled; bilateral tax treaties typically reduce interest to 10% or 0% and royalties to 10% or 5%, depending on the counterparty country and intellectual property characterisation.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File (documentación específica) is mandatory when the Spanish taxpayer's net turnover equals or exceeds EUR 10 million, unless the related-party transactions are de minimis; Master File (documentación del grupo) is required when the consolidated net turnover of the group to which the Spanish entity belongs is at least EUR 45 million; Country-by-Country reporting is separately due for multinational groups with consolidated annual revenue of EUR 750 million or more.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not operate formal offshore-style Economic Substance Regulations as in the UAE or Bermuda; nevertheless, economic substance is decisive under the Spanish General Tax Law anti-abuse rule (art. 15 LGT), the judicial doctrine of beneficial ownership, and the European tax-avoidance directives. A Spanish S.L. engaged in desalination EPC contracting must maintain real local substance: actual offices, staff, managerial decisions, accounting records, and commercial risk; empty pass-through vehicles with no decision-making in Spain risk denial of treaty benefits, recharacterisation, and the imposition of domestic CIT on all attributed income.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing or using false invoices, underreporting construction turnover from seawater desalination EPC works, inflating subcontractor costs, concealing project advances, or fraudulently offsetting loss carryforwards when the evaded amount exceeds EUR 120,000 in any tax year
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty: 50% to 150% of the understated tax plus default interest; criminal sanction under art. 305 Código Penal: imprisonment from 1 to 5 years, fines equal to two to six times the defrauded amount, loss of subsidies or public benefits, publication of the conviction, and disqualification from contracting with public administrations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who cause or acquiesce to the evasion are personally responsible: jointly and subsidiarily liable for the corporate tax debt under arts. 42 and 43 LGT; in criminal proceedings the court may impose travel bans, passport surrender, asset embargoes, and pretrial detention; conviction can result in disqualification from managing Spanish companies and, where the company is insolvent, piercing of the corporate veil against the S.L.'s directors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Artificial Structure / Treaty Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Interposing the Spanish S.L. exclusively to access Spain-Latam double tax treaties, EU directives, or Spanish tax credits without genuine Spanish management or operational substance; zero local staff; board decisions taken abroad; invoices and escrow flows substantially routed through third parties or low-tax seats
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AEAT will apply the general anti-abuse rule (art. 15 LGT), recharacterise the arrangements, disregard the artificial shell, and assess tax at the level of the beneficial owner; late-payment penalty of 50% to 150% of the evaded amount; refusal of treaty/directive relief; administrative sanctions for simulated legal transactions with a penalty of 150% of the evaded tax if the transaction is also considered 'negocio simulado'.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Spanish courts may apply 'levantamiento del velo' (piercing the veil) to hold directors personally liable for the company's tax debts and contractual liabilities when the corporate form has been abused; directors can be declared jointly liable under art. 42 LGT; criminal tax-fraud prosecution is possible if intended evasion exceeds EUR 120,000 and the artificial structure conceals the true taxpayer.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to conduct customer due diligence on the Spanish S.L.'s beneficial owners and project escrow counterparties, failure to register the beneficial owner in the official corporate registry, or failure to file Suspicious Activity Reports (SARs) with SEPBLAC despite red flags in the Swift Wire / project-financing escrow payment rail
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Spanish Law 10/2010, serious breaches attract fines from EUR 60,001 to EUR 6,000,000 or up to ten times the amount involved, plus public reprimand; criminal money laundering under art. 301 Código Penal carries imprisonment of 3 to 6 years and fines up to six times the laundered value for intentional laundering of proceeds derived from criminal activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers face personal criminal prosecution for deliberate involvement; the court may impose travel bans, seizure of personal assets, and surrender of passports; directors can be banned from holding positions in Spanish credit institutions or financial services companies for up to 10 years; the company's non-payment of the AML fine does not extinguish the director's own liability where the breach is attributable to gross negligence or intent.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Not preparing or preserving the Local File or Master File, failure to file Modelo 232 (annual related-party transactions statement), absence of contemporaneous comparability analysis for EPC intercompany services, payments of royalties or interest to non-resident related parties without a valid arm's-length benchmark, or artificial splitting of construction margins between affiliated entities
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AEAT makes a primary and, when required, secondary transfer-pricing adjustment, reassessing the taxable base; non-compliance with documentation obligations triggers specific penalties per article of the CIT Regulations (fixed sanctions per omitted item, with a minimum penalty for non-submission), and the underassessment of tax due results in the 50% to 150% late-payment penalty; conduct may escalate to criminal tax evasion if the adjusted annual tax shortfall exceeds EUR 120,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign Modelo 232 knowing it contains false data or who approve invoicing schemes that have no economic reality face direct criminal liability; they may be declared jointly and severally liable for the full difference between the arm's-length tax and the tax reported; precautionary measures such as travel bans, passport retention, and bank account seizures are available; upon conclusion, directors may be disqualified from managing Spanish entities for a period commensurate with the fraud.
